Electric Touring Bikes: The Current Options

The electric motorcycle market has matured significantly, with several manufacturers now offering machines with genuine touring potential. While none yet match the range and refuelling convenience of petrol touring bikes, the technology has reached a point where planned electric touring is practical and enjoyable.

What to Look For

  • Real-world range — Ignore manufacturer claims based on urban riding. Look for independently tested highway range figures, which are typically 30-40 percent lower than headline numbers.
  • Charging speed — Level 3 DC fast charging capability is essential for touring. Check the maximum charge rate in kW — higher is faster.
  • Charging connector — CCS (Combined Charging System) is the UK standard for DC fast charging. Ensure compatibility with public charging networks.
  • Luggage options — Check what luggage systems are available. Electric bikes have different frame layouts that may not accept standard motorcycle luggage.

Best Electric Touring Bikes 2026

Energica Experia — The first electric motorcycle designed specifically for touring. 420km claimed urban range with a realistic 200km at highway speeds. 22kW DC fast charging reaches 80 percent in about 40 minutes. Comfortable ergonomics, good wind protection, and Moto Guzzi-derived chassis design.

Zero SR/S — Zero's sport-touring model with a 17.3kWh battery. Approximately 130 miles of real-world highway range. Rapid charging capable with optional charge tank. The riding experience is refined and the app connectivity is excellent.

Harley-Davidson LiveWire S2 Del Mar — Harley's electric sportster with touring potential. Approximately 110 miles of mixed riding range. The Arrow architecture is lightweight and agile. Limited luggage options but an engaging riding experience.

BMW CE 04 — Not a traditional tourer but BMW's electric scooter has 130km range and rapid charging. For urban-based short touring between cities, it is practical and futuristic.

Running Costs

Electric motorcycles are dramatically cheaper to run than petrol equivalents. Electricity costs roughly 2-3p per mile compared to 8-12p per mile for petrol. Servicing costs are lower too — no oil changes, no chain maintenance, fewer brake pad replacements thanks to regenerative braking. Insurance can be higher due to specialist repair requirements.

The electric touring experience is genuinely different — the silence, the instant torque, and the smooth power delivery create a meditative quality to riding that petrol bikes cannot replicate. Many riders who try electric touring find it addictive.

Buying Considerations

Electric motorcycles depreciate faster than petrol equivalents due to rapid technology improvements. Consider whether the current technology meets your needs or whether waiting another year or two for improved range and charging speed makes more financial sense. faq.q: Which electric motorcycle is best for touring?
faq.a: The Energica Experia is the standout because it was designed specifically for touring, offering around 200km of highway range, 22kW DC fast charging to 80 percent in about 40 minutes, comfortable ergonomics and proper wind protection. The Zero SR/S is a strong sport-touring alternative. For pure touring capability in 2026, the Experia leads the field by a clear margin.

faq.q: Why should I ignore manufacturer range claims?
faq.a: Headline range figures are usually based on gentle urban riding, which bears little relation to touring. Independently tested highway range is typically 30 to 40 percent lower because motorway speeds sap the battery quickly. When comparing bikes for touring, look for real-world highway figures rather than the optimistic combined or city numbers in the brochure.

faq.q: What charging connector do I need?
faq.a: CCS, the Combined Charging System, is the UK standard for DC fast charging and the connector you want for touring. It gives access to the widest range of public rapid chargers along motorways and A-roads. Check that any bike you consider supports CCS and note its maximum charge rate in kW, as a higher figure means shorter stops.

faq.q: Do electric bikes cost less to run?
faq.a: Considerably less. Electricity costs roughly 2 to 3p per mile against 8 to 12p for petrol, and there are no oil changes, no chain maintenance and fewer brake pad replacements thanks to regenerative braking. The main offsets are potentially higher insurance and faster depreciation, so the overall saving depends on how many miles you cover.
